Yes. Your ZIP contains :codex-file-citation{path="C:/Users/vansh/Downloads/preflight/preflight/SESSION_OVERVIEW.pdf" purpose="source"}, a five-page guide to the **Goghl.ai SDE 2 and SDE 3 coding assessment**. The actual project brief and checker are released when the assessment starts.

## What you’ll do

You’ll have **2 hours on a group call** to build a small product using Node.js or TypeScript, React, MongoDB, and Redis. You get **10 minutes to read and start services, 100 minutes to build, and 10 minutes to run the final check and submit**. Join five minutes early.

The brief deliberately asks for more than fits in the time. They’re grading what you prioritize, how you verify it, and whether your app behaves correctly through network problems, process restarts, and multiple instances running at once. You can run their checker as often as you like.

## The rules

- **Work alone.** AI tools are allowed and expected. Documentation, search, your own notes and snippets, and any Node framework or libraries are allowed. Ask assessment questions in the shared channel so everyone sees the answers.
- **Export every AI conversation you use** into the repository’s `ai-logs/` folder.
- **Commit at least every 15 minutes.**
- **Create a new GitHub repository on assessment day.** Keep it private while you build, make it public when you submit, and leave it public and unchanged for **14 days**.
- **Push your final commit and send the form before the two-hour cutoff.** They take a snapshot at the cutoff, so later pushes won’t count.

## What you submit

- **GitHub repo** with your code and commit history, a README that lets someone run it from a clean clone, a half-page note explaining your decisions, your last checker report, and your AI transcripts.
- **Submission form** with your name, email, repo URL, final commit ID, and the AI tools you used.

## What to prepare

At least a day before, check that **Node 22, Git, and Docker Desktop** work, that Docker has about **4 GB of memory free**, and that you can push to GitHub from your terminal. Pre-pull `mongo:7`, `redis:7-alpine`, and `node:22-alpine`. Elasticsearch `8.15.3` is optional. Run `node doctor.js --preflight` and address any `WARN` results. Make sure your AI tool can export conversations.

If you’re shortlisted, there’s a **30-minute follow-up** where you’ll explain your decisions and debug a failure in your own submission, including any code AI helped write.

You’re my AI coding assistant for the Goghl.ai SDE assessment. I’ll supervise and review the work. Take ownership of implementation, verification, Git commits, and submission prep in this workspace.

Assessment start and hard submission cutoff, including timezone: [fill in]

2. Build a working end-to-end slice first. Run the provided checker early and use its results to drive the next changes. Prioritize correctness under the failure scenarios in the brief, including network issues, process restarts, and concurrent instances where applicable. Record assumptions, tradeoffs, and unfinished requirements honestly.
3. Track elapsed time from the assessment start. Commit progress at least every 15 minutes during the build without waiting for me to remind you. Use meaningful commit messages. Keep the repository private during the build. If a sign-in, approval, or missing input blocks you, tell me what you need and continue independent work.

5. Stop feature work when the final 10 minutes begin. Run the full checker, save its report, verify the required deliverables, and push the final commit. Make the repo public at submission time once I give the go-ahead. Verify the public repo URL and final commit SHA, then give me those details and the list of AI tools used so I can submit the form before the cutoff.
